paragraphs: The morning starts with a coordination meeting about engineering changes. Back at the workstation, the Drafter updates CAD files, adjusts elevations, and checks standards. Midday brings drawing coordination with structural and building-services teams to resolve conflicts. The afternoon includes BIM clash detection and a new issue set, followed by archiving and site questions.

In one sentence: turn a design into drawings that can be built. Work includes construction drawings, dimensions and materials, standards checks, discipline coordination, revisions, and final drawing issues for the site.

This work combines attention to detail, order, and willingness to learn software. Drawings must be clear and standards correct because one wrong line can cause site rework.

This career suits people who can sit for long periods, notice detail, and value order in drawings. Turning a disorganized idea into clear lines and then seeing the drawing become a real building creates strong satisfaction.
Practical, orderly, and analytical preferences (Realistic R + Conventional C + Investigative I).
If you are careful, patient, and treat drawing accuracy as the standard, architectural drafting provides a strong entry into standards-driven engineering work.
